title: Execution of a decree — the main roads

steps.title: Which court executes?
steps.text: Court that passed the decree (incl. first-instance court after appeal) or the court to which it is sent

steps.title: Within time?
steps.text: First application within 3 years; fresh applications within 6 years (fraud / force excepted)

steps.title: Application and notice
steps.text: Tabular application; notice if > 1 year or against legal representative

steps.title: Objections
steps.text: Judgment-debtor: s. 47 after deposit (r. 23-A); third party: claim within 1 year (r. 58)

steps.title: Mode chosen by decree-holder
steps.text: Delivery, attachment and sale, arrest and detention, receiver, other

steps.title: Attachment and sale
steps.text: Exemptions; proclamation; 25% deposit, balance in 15 days; set aside rr. 89–91

steps.title: Possession
steps.text: Actual or symbolic; resistance and dispossession inquiries; police assistance

steps.title: Satisfaction and distribution
steps.text: Payment certified; rateable distribution among money decree-holders

rootSub: all three must co-exist; relief is equitable and discretionary

children.title: 1. Prima facie case
children.text: A serious, bona fide question to be tried on the plaint, documents and affidavits — not proof of title (Dalpat Kumar; American Cyanamid)

children.title: 2. Balance of convenience
children.text: Greater hardship if refused than if granted; when even, preserve the status quo

children.title: 3. Irreparable loss
children.text: Injury that money cannot adequately repair — sale of unique property, demolition, loss of goodwill

title: Objections in execution — who, under which rule, and the result

cards.title: Judgment-debtor objects to execution
bullets: Not considered without deposit / security (O. XXI r. 23-A)

cards.title: Third party claims attached property
bullets: O. XXI r. 58: within reasonable time / 1 year of attachment
Prove title at date of attachment (r. 59)
Decided fully; no separate suit (r. 62); r. 63 omitted

cards.title: Decree-holder / purchaser resisted
bullets: By judgment-debtor → possession + 30 days' prison (r. 98; s. 74)
Bona fide own-account possessor → dismissed (r. 99), title decided (r. 103)

cards.title: Stranger dispossessed
bullets: Restored if in possession on own account (r. 101)

title: Sale of immovable property in execution

steps.title: Attachment
steps.text: Prohibitory order proclaimed and affixed; later transfers void against attachment

steps.title: Proclamation of sale
steps.text: After notice to parties; encumbrances, revenue, amount due stated

steps.title: Waiting period
steps.text: No sale within 30 days (immovable) / 15 days (movable) without consent

steps.title: Auction
steps.text: Decree-holder bids only with leave; officers cannot bid; co-sharer preference

steps.title: Deposit and balance
steps.text: 25% immediately; balance before court closes on the 15th day; else forfeiture and re-sale

steps.title: Objections to sale
steps.text: r. 89 deposit (5% + amount); r. 90 irregularity / fraud + injury (deposit ≤ 20%); r. 91 no saleable interest — 30 days

steps.title: Confirmation and certificate
steps.text: Sale absolute; certificate; title vests from date of sale

q.ask: Is it a decree (incl. deemed decree) of a court of original jurisdiction?
q.yes: First appeal as of right (s. 96) — 30 days to DJ / 90 days to HC; not if consent decree (s. 96(3)).
Second appeal to the High Court on the three grounds of s. 100 only (90 days).

q.ask: Is the order listed in s. 104 or O. XLIII r. 1?
q.yes: Appeal from order (s. 104) — no second appeal (s. 104(2)).

q.ask: Is there a jurisdictional error, illegality or material irregularity in a case decided where no appeal lies?
q.yes: Revision (s. 115) — DJ or HC, one only, 90 days; or raise in appeal from decree (s. 105).

q.ask: Is there an error apparent on the record, new evidence, or a clerical slip?
q.yes: Review (s. 114; O. XLVII — 90 days) or s. 152 correction (any time).
q.no: Fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction? Apply under s. 12(2) to the court of the final decree.
